strengths: Novel and insightful perspective: Introducing Kinetic Path Energy (KPE) as a trajectory-level, action-inspired diagnostic provides a fresh lens for analyzing conditional flow matching. It is computationally zero-overhead during ODE sampling and offers fine-grained insight that endpoint-only metrics (like FID) fail to capture.

Rigorous theoretical analysis: The paper establishes a sound mathematical foundation connecting instantaneous kinetic energy to the negative log-density of the bridge mixture under posterior dominance (Theorem 4.2 / Theorem B.1). Furthermore, the derivation of the terminal-time singularity and kinetic energy blow-up in empirical flow matching (EFM, Proposition 5.2) cleanly explains the mechanics of memorization in non-regularized empirical regimes.

Thorough empirical validation of diagnostic claims: The correlation of KPE with semantic fidelity (CLIP score/margin across CFG scales) and local sparsity (via synthetic 2D datasets, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-256 across multiple feature representations) is systematically documented and statistically verified.

Clear narrative and well-motivated inference intervention: The transition from the 'energy proxy for fidelity' to the 'extreme energy memorization paradox' leads naturally to the Goldilocks principle and the proposed Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS) method.
weaknesses: Divergence between theoretical setting and practical neural models: The terminal kinetic blow-up and singular behavior are derived for the exact empirical closed-form velocity field (EFM). However, as shown in Figure 6, neural network velocity fields (Vanilla FM) have finite capacity and smooth activations, exhibiting no unbounded power spikes. While overfitted neural networks exhibit increased late-time KPE (Figure 7a), the literal terminal divergence strictly applies to EFM. Clarifying the gap between the theoretical pole in EFM and the bounded behavior in neural parameterizations would strengthen the narrative.

Modest empirical gains on large-scale benchmarks: While KTS demonstrates noticeable memorization reductions on the intentionally constrained 1,024-sample CelebA benchmark, the generation quality improvements on ImageNet-256 (Table 5) are very modest (FID goes from 11.70 to 11.63 in the balanced configuration). Furthermore, memorization metrics ($F_{\text{mem}}$) are omitted for ImageNet-256, leaving the real-world impact on memorization in web-scale datasets unverified.

Theoretical implications of uncoupled velocity rescaling: As noted in Section 6.1, KTS scales the velocity vector by $\eta(t)$ while keeping the time argument $t$ fixed in $v_\theta(x, t)$. Although Proposition I.2 provides a worst-case Grönwall stability bound showing the terminal trajectory deviation is small, scaling velocity without reparameterizing the conditioning time $t$ technically violates the continuity equation governing the probability flow. A deeper discussion on how this off-manifold perturbation interacts with the true transport plan would be valuable.
Minor presentation slip: In Appendix K, Figure 15 is captioned as 'African Elephant (ImageNet-256)', but the visual display clearly depicts red pandas.

strengths: Conceptual Novelty: Introducing Kinetic Path Energy (KPE) as a trajectory-level, action-inspired diagnostic provides an insightful physical perspective on flow matching, moving beyond endpoint-only aggregate metrics (like FID).

Sound Theoretical Grounding: The paper establishes a rigorous analytical link between instantaneous kinetic energy and local negative log-density of the bridge mixture under posterior dominance (Theorem 4.2 / Theorem B.1), supported by complete proofs.

Mechanistic Explanation of Memorization: The paper identifies and formalizes the 1/(1-t) terminal singularity in empirical flow matching (EFM) as the driver of late-time energy spikes and memorization (Proposition 5.2), providing a clear dynamical mechanism for why over-optimizing regression loss leads to training set replication.

Practical and Training-Free Method: Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS) is conceptually neat, simple to implement without retraining, and backed by a Gronwall stability bound (Proposition I.2) and ablation studies across solvers, step counts, and schedule forms.
weaknesses: Limited Scale of Memorization Experiments: The memorization and anti-memorization evaluations are primarily validated on an artificial, downscaled testbed (CelebA at 32x32 grayscale with only 1,024 training samples). It remains unclear how well KTS prevents memorization in larger-scale, modern text-to-image or high-resolution flow matching models where memorization manifests more subtly.

Marginal Gains on Large-Scale Generation: On ImageNet-256 (Table 5), the quantitative improvements from KTS over baseline FM are quite modest (FID improves from 11.70 to 11.63 in the balanced configuration, or 11.59 with a sacrifice in recall), suggesting that while the method is harmless and conceptually sound, its practical impact on standard generative benchmarks is incremental.

Posterior Dominance Applicability: The core theoretical result (Theorem 4.2) relies on the posterior dominance condition (one mixture component weight >= 1 - epsilon). In high-density or multimodal transition regions (especially at intermediate times t), this assumption may be violated, making the energy-density equivalence less descriptive along the entire trajectory.

Minor Presentation Glitch: In Figure 15 in the appendix, the caption reads 'African Elephant (ImageNet-256)', but the displayed images are clearly red pandas, indicating an errant class label in the qualitative section.

strengths: Conceptual motivation: Investigating generative sampling through the trajectory-level lens of Kinetic Path Energy (KPE) provides an interesting physical perspective that moves beyond trajectory-blind evaluation metrics.

Comprehensive empirical visualizations: The authors provide extensive empirical analyses across synthetic 2D datasets, CIFAR-10, CelebA, and ImageNet-256, examining the relationship between KPE, local density, and semantic metrics.

Detailed appendix: The manuscript includes thorough derivations, a Grönwall-type perturbation analysis for velocity scaling, and sensitivity analyses regarding discretization schemes and neighborhood parameters.
weaknesses: Soundness of Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS): KTS rescales the velocity vector field by a factor $\eta(t)$ during Euler integration while preserving the model's explicit time conditioning $t$. This breaks the mathematical consistency of the underlying probability flow ODE ($\dot{x} = v_\theta(x, t)$) and violates marginal preservation. The sampler no longer follows the continuity equation of the learned data transport.

Mechanistic explanation of memorization reduction: The reduction in memorization ($F_{\text{mem}}$) via late-phase velocity damping ($\beta_0 > 0$) appears to be an artifact of numerical undershooting. By dampening late-time velocity, trajectories simply terminate before reaching the discrete training atoms in heavily overfitted regimes. As shown in Table 4, increasing $\beta_0$ to $0.02$ causes the FID to degrade catastrophically from 16.68 to 86.56, highlighting that this damping acts primarily as an unprincipled endpoint truncation rather than genuine generalization.

Marginal empirical gains on standard benchmarks: On ImageNet-256 (Table 5), the improvements from KTS over standard Flow Matching are negligible (FID drops from 11.70 to 11.63, a 0.07 change evaluated on 10k samples; CLIP score changes from 24.11 to 24.20; Precision/Recall shift by $\le 0.003$). The memorization evaluation relies exclusively on an artificial toy setup (1,024 grayscale images of CelebA $32\times 32$ overfitted for 2M iterations), leaving the practical utility of KTS on standard generative tasks unproven.

Limited novelty and strong assumptions in theoretical analysis: The $1/(1-t)$ singularity and terminal blow-up in empirical flow matching (EFM) are already established properties in recent literature (e.g., Bertrand et al., 2025; Bonnaire et al., 2025). Furthermore, Theorem 4.2 relies on a strict 'posterior dominance' assumption ($\lambda_{i^*} \ge 1 - \varepsilon$), which effectively reduces the mixture to a single Gaussian component where the relation $\|\nabla \log p\|^2 \asymp -\log p$ is standard and elementary.

Presentation and quality control issues: In Appendix K, Figure 15 is captioned as 'African Elephant (ImageNet-256)', but the visual display depicts red pandas. Additionally, the empirical analysis in Section 4.1 uses forward Euler with only NFE = 10 on ImageNet-256, where large integration errors may confound the observed kinetic energy measurements.

strengths: Original and insightful perspective: The paper introduces Kinetic Path Energy (KPE) as a trajectory-level, action-inspired diagnostic for flow matching, bridging classical mechanics / optimal transport intuition with per-sample generative dynamics.

Solid theoretical analysis: Theorem 4.2 (and Appendix B) establishes a clean analytical connection between instantaneous kinetic energy and local negative log-density under the posterior dominance regime. The derivation of the structural terminal-time 1/(1-t) singularity in empirical flow matching (Proposition 5.2 / Lemma 5.1) rigorously explains the terminal power blow-up and its link to memorization.

Comprehensive empirical investigation: The paper provides extensive empirical support across 2D toy setups, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-256, verifying both the semantic fidelity correlation and the negative correlation between trajectory energy and data density.

Practical training-free intervention: Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS) is computationally lightweight, training-free, and directly motivated by the two-phase 'Goldilocks' analysis (launching early, dampening late).
weaknesses: Marginal gains on large-scale benchmarks: While KTS demonstrates noticeable memorization suppression on the small-sample CelebA benchmark, the improvements on standard ImageNet-256 (Table 4) are minimal (e.g., FID drops from 11.70 to 11.63 for the balanced setting; CLIP score increases slightly from 24.11 to 24.20). The practical utility of KTS on large-scale, well-regularized models remains somewhat limited.

Artificial memorization setting: The CelebA experiments specifically use a downsampled, 1024-image grayscale subset trained for 2M iterations to induce pathological memorization. It remains unclear how KTS affects standard models trained on full-scale data distributions where terminal memorization is not the dominant failure mode.

Theoretical scope of posterior dominance: Theorem 4.2 and its integrated trajectory form (Eq. 11) rely on the posterior dominance condition (where a single training point dominates the responsibility weights). While this condition naturally holds near $t \to 1$, it clearly fails in the early sampling regime ($t \approx 0$) where responsibilities are diffuse across training samples. The transition between these regimes is not formally addressed in the integral bound.
Minor presentation slip: In Appendix H, Figure 15 is captioned as 'African Elephant (ImageNet-256)', but the displayed images clearly depict red pandas.

strengths: Original and physically grounded perspective: Analyzing individual flow matching generation paths through Kinetic Path Energy (KPE)—an action-like per-sample diagnostic—provides an intuitive, zero-overhead framework to understand trajectory dynamics beyond global, endpoint-only metrics like FID.

Solid theoretical analysis connecting energy and density: Theorem 4.2 (and the detailed proofs in Appendix B) establishes a formal relationship between instantaneous kinetic energy and negative log-density under posterior dominance, showing how optimal velocity decomposes into score and drift components.

Rigorous explanation of memorization in empirical flow matching: Lemma 5.1 and Proposition 5.2 convincingly demonstrate how the regression-optimal closed-form velocity field inherently develops a terminal 1/(1-t) singularity, clarifying the mechanistic link between extreme terminal kinetic energy and dataset memorization.

Comprehensive qualitative and synthetic validation: The 2D synthetic experiments (dense-sparse, multiscale clusters, sandwich) nicely illustrate the theoretical claims regarding trajectory power, cumulative energy, and density stratification.
weaknesses: Limited and artificial benchmark for KTS evaluation: The memorization mitigation capability of Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS) is demonstrated primarily on an artificially constrained setup (1,024 grayscale 32x32 CelebA images overtrained for 2M steps). While motivated by prior work on memorization, it remains unclear how well KTS generalizes to standard, full-scale training regimes and modern large-scale benchmarks where severe overfitting is not deliberately induced.

Marginal empirical improvement on large-scale models: On ImageNet-256 using SiT-XL/2 (Table 4), the performance difference between baseline FM (FID 11.70) and balanced KTS (FID 11.63) is negligible, and several KTS configurations degrade FID (e.g., up to 12.45). This suggests that KTS provides limited practical benefit on properly regularized, large-scale pretrained models.

Heuristic nature of KTS velocity rescaling: Rescaling the velocity field via time-dependent factors (1 + α(t) and 1 - β(t)) modifies the ODE integration without guarantees that the terminal marginal distribution remains aligned with the target data distribution. A more theoretically grounded velocity reparameterization or time-warping scheme would strengthen the methodology.

Proxy density estimation in high dimensions: As acknowledged by the authors, estimating density on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet via PCA on 22 hand-crafted visual descriptors followed by k-NN/KDE is highly sensitive to representation choices, weakening the direct empirical support for the energy-density relationship on complex real-world data.
Minor presentation errors: In Appendix H, Figure 15 is captioned as 'African Elephant', but the generated images clearly display red pandas.

strengths: Compelling conceptual framing: The paper provides a clean, physically grounded framework by examining Kinetic Path Energy (KPE) as a per-sample, path-level diagnostic for flow-based generative models.

Solid theoretical analysis: Theorem 4.2 / Theorem B.1 effectively formalizes the relationship between instantaneous trajectory energy and the negative log-density under the posterior dominance regime. Furthermore, Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 5.1 rigorously characterize why the regression-optimal empirical flow matching (EFM) exhibits late-time velocity singularities and energy blow-up.

Insightful diagnosis of the 'energy paradox': Differentiating between early-stage kinetic effort (which correlates with semantic clarity and diversity) and terminal energy spikes (which induce memorization and trajectory collapse) provides fresh insight into flow dynamics.

Practical and lightweight intervention: Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS) is training-free and intuitive, modulating early vs. late velocity to balance semantic exploration against terminal memorization.
weaknesses: Marginal empirical gains on large-scale benchmarks: On ImageNet-256 (Table 4), the performance deltas between baseline FM and KTS are very subtle (e.g., baseline FID 11.70 vs. best KTS FID 11.59, with recall declining from 0.655 to 0.630; CLIP score 24.11 vs. 24.20–24.34). It is unclear whether these differences are statistically meaningful or practically impactful at scale.

Evaluation setup for memorization is limited: The memorization reduction experiments are largely conducted in an artificial setting (CelebA 32x32 subsampled to 1,024 images). Demonstrating that KTS mitigates real memorization risks in modern web-scale or moderately sized text-to-image/unconditional models without severely degrading fidelity remains unverified.

Missing crucial comparison with simple early stopping / truncated sampling: In flow matching and diffusion literature, a well-known heuristic to prevent terminal memorization or singularity collapse is simple early stopping / truncation at $t = 1 - \epsilon$. Because the late-phase damping $\eta(t) = 1 - \beta(t)$ essentially shrinks the net distance traversed near $t=1$, a comparison against simple early termination (e.g., integrating up to $t = 0.98$ or $0.95$) is essential to prove that soft-landing is superior.

Heuristic density estimation proxies: High-dimensional density estimation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet is performed by projecting 22 hand-crafted features down to 2D via PCA before applying k-NN/KDE. While the authors acknowledge this limitation in Section 4.2, the empirical conclusions regarding manifold rarity in real image distributions remain contingent on this aggressive low-dimensional projection.
